'''Zilingo''' was an ecommerce fashion platform founded in 2015 by Ankiti Bose and Dhruv Kapoor, with operations spanning India, Singapore, Indonesia, [[Hong Kong]], Thailand, Philippines, [[Australia]] and the [[United States]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/most-powerful-women/riding-a-unicorn/story/379321.html|title=Riding A Unicorn- Business News|website=www.businesstoday.in|date=16 September 2019 |access-date=2019-10-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/ranawehbe/2019/05/19/aiming-for-zillions-zilingo-finds-a-niche-in-asias-crowded-e-commerce-market/|title=Aiming For Zillions: Zilingo Finds A Niche In Asia's Crowded E-Commerce Market|first=Rana Wehbe|last=Watson|website=Forbes}}</ref> The company once valued at close to one billion dollars<ref name="Subramaniam">{{Cite web |last=Subramaniam |first=Nikhil |date=2023-04-21 |title=Zilingo’s Collapse: Inside Ankiti Bose’s Multimillion-Dollar Implosion |url=https://inc42.com/features/zilingo-ankiti-bose-multimillion-dollar-catastrophe/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=Inc42 Media |language=en}}</ref> ceased operations in 2022 amidst scandal and mismanagement.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why did Zilingo fail? How Scandal and Mismanagement KILLED Zilingo! |url=https://buildd.co/startup/failure-stories/why-did-zilingo-fail |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=buildd |language=en}}</ref>  It sold its tech assets to Swiss firm [[buyogo.ch|Buyogo]] in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kashyap |first=Hemant |date=2023-01-24 |title=Zilingo Sells nCinga, Tech Assets To Swiss Ecommerce Enabler Buyogo AG |url=https://inc42.com/buzz/zilingo-ncinga-tech-assets-german-ecommerce-enabler-buyogo-ag/?_gl=1*orivwy*_ga*bC1zUnlXOWRwTlhpNGFXaWZGUF9qM0pkSzV0bGs0MDU4bDZTTjQ0dHlQcDRWLVRkMklIZUxFSlU0REFwOUF2YQ..*_ga_67F2T4M6Z5*MTczNjI4Mzg0Ny4zLjEuMTczNjI4NDE5My4wLjAuMA.. |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=Inc42 Media |language=en}}</ref> It entered liquidation in February 2023<ref>{{Cite web |title=Singapore Business Directory |url=https://www.sgpbusiness.com/company/Zilingo-Pte-Ltd |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=Singapore Business Directory |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=20 January 2023 |title=Singapore's Zilingo to Liquidate After Crisis at Fashion Startup |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-01-20/singapore-s-zilingo-to-liquidate-after-crisis-at-fashion-startup?srnd=prognosis&leadSource=uverify%20wall |access-date=20 January 2023 |website=[[Bloomberg News]]}}</ref> with sources indicating there was nothing left to be recovered.<ref name="Subramaniam"/>  Lawsuits related to the implosion of the business remain ongoing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-03 |title=Ankiti Bose, ex-Zilingo CEO, embarks on legal battle with former partners: A closer look at her journey |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/life/lifestyle-ankiti-bose-ex-zilingo-ceo-embarks-on-legal-battle-with-former-partners-a-closer-look-at-her-journey-3475704/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==

===Founding and growth===
Zilingo, a play on the word "zillion", was established in 2015 by two founders of Indian origin, Ankiti Bose<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hindisuccesswiki.com/ankiti-bose-zilingo/|title=Real Truth Behind Zilingo in Hindi- अंकिति बोस-Zilingo का पर्दाफाश}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and Dhruv Kapoor.<ref name="StraitsTimes">{{cite news |last1=Woo |first1=Alyssa |title=Selling online gets easy |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/lifestyle/selling-online-gets-easy |access-date=19 July 2018 |publisher=Straits Times |date=17 August 2017}}</ref> The idea came from when Bose was on holiday in [[Bangkok]] and noticed that many of the small and medium-sized shops had no online presence.<ref name="BusinessTImes">{{cite news |last1=Chiang |first1=Tay Suan |title=Ankiti Bose |url=https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/lifestyle/weekend-interview/ankiti-bose |access-date=19 July 2018 |publisher=Business Times |date=3 June 2017}}</ref><ref name="ISEA">{{cite news |last1=Morente |first1=Tricia V. |title=Zilingo: The Singapore-Based e-Merchant of Small Things is Getting Bigger |url=http://inc-asean.com/editor-picks/zilingo-singapore-based-e-merchant-small-things-getting-bigger/ |access-date=19 July 2018 |publisher=Inc. Southeast Asia |date=13 September 2017}}</ref>

It began with seed funding from [[Sequoia Capital|Sequoia India]]<ref name="TechCrunch18">{{cite news |last1=Russell |first1=Jon |title=Zilingo raises $18M for its fashion ecommerce service in Southeast Asia |url=https://techcrunch.com/2017/09/12/zilingo-raises-18m/ |access-date=19 July 2018 |publisher=Tech Crunch |date=12 September 2017}}</ref> and raised an additional $8 million in a Series A funding round in September 2016.<ref name="TechCrunch8">{{cite news |last1=Russell |first1=Jon |title=Zilingo lands $8M for its marketplace for fashion sellers in Southeast Asia |url=https://techcrunch.com/2016/09/05/zilingo-lands-8m-for-its-marketplace-for-fashion-sellers-in-southeast-asia/ |access-date=19 July 2018 |publisher=Tech Crunch |date=5 September 2016}}</ref> It raised an additional $18 million in 2017 in a Series B round<ref name="TechCrunch18"/> and $54 million in a Series C round in 2018.<ref name="TechCrunch54">{{cite news |last1=Russell |first1=Jon |title=Southeast Asia fashion startup Zilingo continues its meteoric rise with $54M Series C |url=https://techcrunch.com/2018/04/04/zilingo-raises-54-million/ |access-date=19 July 2018 |publisher=Tech Crunch |date=4 April 2018}}</ref>

The company started off as a B2C long-tail fashion marketplace leveraging Southeast Asia's growing internet connectivity to bring small merchants from the street markets of Bangkok and Jakarta into the e-commerce fold.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/02/11/zilingo-raises-226m/|title=E-commerce startup Zilingo raises $226M to digitize Asia's fashion supply chain|date=12 February 2019 }}</ref>

Zilingo later expanded focus towards B2B opportunities.<ref name=":0"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pymnts.com/news/b2b-payments/2019/zilingo-venture-capital-funding-supply-chain/|title=One thing that's become very clear to us is there's a lot of value [in] making the supply chain efficient, instead of giving out discounts and doing crazy marketing|date=13 February 2019}}</ref> This included products designed to help merchants and manufacturers manage their e-commerce business including inventory management, sales tracking, financing, sourcing procurement, and a ‘style hunter’ for identifying upcoming fashion trends.<ref name=":0" />

Expansion efforts led the company to be valued at nearly one billion dollars by 2019.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-02-12/this-near-1-billion-startup-is-led-by-a-27-year-old-female-ceo|title=How a 27-Year-Old CEO Built a Near $1 Billion Fashion Startup|date=2019-07-21|access-date=2019-07-22|language=en}}</ref> Their fashion platform took a cut whenever it was used to broker a deal or make a sale,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.techinasia.com/singaporebased-ecommerce-startup-zilingo-winner-uschina-trade-war|title=Tech in Asia - Connecting Asia's startup ecosystem|website=www.techinasia.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-01}}</ref> as part of the company vision of making the fashion supply chain a ''levelled playing field''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vulcanpost.com/657807/zilingo-online-fashion-marketplace/|title=At Zilingo, we keep the merchant at the centre of everything. We have seen the pain points of some of these enterprises first-hand — not being able to improve their margins or grow any further due to lack of technology access and capital. Meanwhile, big international brands continue to grow aggressively|website=vulcanpost.com|date=11 March 2019}}</ref>

In September 2017, Zilingo was shipping to eight countries and had added 5,000 new merchants in the previous twelve months.<ref name="TechCrunch18" /> By September 2019 the company was generating 80% of its revenue from B2B operations.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-09-20|title=Zilingo's CEO on Supply Chain, U.S. Expansion, Sustainability|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2019-09-20/zilingo-s-ceo-on-supply-chain-u-s-expansion-sustainability-video|access-date=2019-10-01|website=Bloomberg.com}}</ref>

In 2019, the company raised $226 million in a Series D round from existing investors Sequoia India, Burda Capital, [[Sofina]] with Singapore's sovereign fund [[Temasek Holdings]] joining the tech-platform's capital table.<ref name=":0" /> The latest round took the tech-platform to US$308 million from investors, making it one of Southeast Asia's highest capitalised startups.<ref name=":0" />

The company closed its US and Australia offices in 2020, to focus on business in Asia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/garage/axed-zilingo-workers-upset-by-how-layoffs-were-handled|title=Axed Zilingo workers upset by how layoffs were handled|date=2020-04-21|website=The Business Times|language=en|access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref> In July 2020, a second round of terminations was carried out in Thailand, India, and Indonesia offices, with an estimated additional 12% of employees being laid off globally. CFO James Perry resigned following the rounds of downsizing.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/garage/zilingo-cfo-james-perry-resigns-to-return-to-citigroup-for-tech-deals |title=Zilingo CFO James Perry resigns to return to Citigroup for tech deals |date=October 27, 2020 |orig-date=September 28, 2020 |website=www.businesstimes.com.sg}}</ref>

=== Dismissal of CEO ===

On March 30 whistleblowers approached the Zilingo board reporting a series of unexplained payments approved by Ankiti Bose to companies with no connection to Zilingo operations.<ref name="Subramaniam"/>  On 31 March 2022, Bose was suspended as CEO.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zilingo finally fires CEO Ankiti Bose after 51-day suspension—for 'insubordination' |url=https://fortune.com/2022/05/20/zilingo-fires-ceo-ankiti-bose-after-51-day-suspension-insubordination/ |website=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] |access-date=8 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Temasek-backed Zilingo suspends CEO amid accounting probe - Bloomberg News |url=https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/temasek-backed-zilingo-suspends-ceo-amid-accounting-probe-bloomberg-news |website=[[Nasdaq]] |access-date=12 April 2022}}</ref> On 20 May 2022 Bose was fired from Zilingo after independent forensics firm investigated the financial irregularities.<ref name="u122">{{cite web | last1=Lee | first1=Yoolim | last2=Ramli | first2=David | title=Zilingo Fires CEO in Escalating Clash at Singapore Startup | website=NDTV | date=2022-05-24 | url=https://www.ndtvprofit.com/business/zilingo-fires-ceo-as-clash-over-embattled-startup-escalates-10108203 | access-date=2026-07-26}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Zilingo Fires CEO as Clash Over Embattled Startup Escalates |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-05-20/zilingo-fires-ceo-as-clash-over-embattled-startup-escalates |website=Bloomberg News |date=20 May 2022 |access-date=20 May 2022}}</ref>

=== Management buyout ===
On 20 June 2022, the cofounders of Zilingo, Dhruv Kapoor and Ankiti Bose, sent a proposal to the board for a [[Management buyout|management buyout (MBO)]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Burgos |first=Jonathan |title=Zilingo Cofounders Propose To Buyout Financially Troubled Startup |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonathanburgos/2022/06/20/zilingo-cofounders-propose-to-buyout-financially-troubled-startup/ |access-date=2022-06-21 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> making a last ditch effort to buy the embattled fashion platform.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-06-19 |title=Zilingo Founders Make Surprise Buyout Offer for Startup |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-19/zilingo-co-founders-make-surprise-buyout-offer-for-startup?embed |access-date=2025-01-07 |work=Bloomberg.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Lawsuits===
In April 2024 Bose filed a $100 million dollar defamation lawsuit against investor Mahesh Murthy for an article he wrote in Outlook Business magazine.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Livemint |date=2023-04-24 |title=Investor sued by Zilingo founder for highlighting misuse of money by CEO Ankiti |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/start-ups/investor-mahesh-murthy-sued-by-zilingo-founder-for-highlighting-misuse-of-money-by-ceo-ankiti-bose-11682293664163.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230526101030/https://www.livemint.com/companies/start-ups/investor-mahesh-murthy-sued-by-zilingo-founder-for-highlighting-misuse-of-money-by-ceo-ankiti-bose-11682293664163.html |archive-date=2023-05-26 |access-date=2025-01-07 |work=mint |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> In April 2024, she accused Dhruv Kapoor (co-founder) and Aadi Vaidya (ex-COO) of fraud, criminal intimidation and sexual harassment.<ref name="y774">{{cite web | last=Desk | first=TOI Tech | title=Zilingo's Ankiti Bose alleges sexual harassment against co-founder; inappropriate behavior and more that FIR claims | website=The Times of India | date=2024-04-25 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/zilingos-ankiti-bose-alleges-sexual-harassment-against-co-founder-inappropriate-behavior-and-more-that-fir-claims/articleshow/109572800.cms | access-date=2026-07-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=24 Apr 2024 |title=Zilingo ex-CEO Ankiti Bose files FIR against co-founder: 'Threatened, deceived me, attributed errors' |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business/zilingo-ex-ceo-ankiti-bose-files-fir-against-co-founder-threatened-deceived-me-attributed-errors-101713941931652.html |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-04-24 |title=Zilingo's Ankiti Bose files FIR against cofounder Dhruv Kapoor |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/startups/zilingo-ex-ceo-ankiti-bose-files-sexual-harassment-case-against-cofounder-ex-coo/articleshow/109565206.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-01-07 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> 

 
In April 2021, one of Zilingo's primary investor citing "significant financial regularities" indicated an intent to sue Bose,<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2023-05-01 |title=Trouble for Ankiti Bose as Zilingo investors indicate legal action against the ousted CEO |url=https://internationalfinance.com/markets/trouble-ankiti-bose-zilingo-investors-legal-action-ousted-ceo/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=International Finance |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-27 |title=Zilingo investors mulls legal action against ex-CEO Ankiti Bose |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/industry-vc-firm-burda-investments-mulls-legal-action-against-ex-zilingo-ceo-ankiti-bose-3064540/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref> while in May 2024 Bose filed a further defamation lawsuit against Kapoor and Vaidya.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-03 |title=Zilingo's Ex-CEO Ankiti Bose files fresh lawsuit against Dhruv Kapoor, Aadi Vaidya for alleged defamation |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/zilingos-ex-ceo-ankiti-bose-files-fresh-lawsuit-against-dhruv-kapoor-aadi-vaidya-for-alleged-defamation-428241-2024-05-03 |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=Business Today |language=en}}</ref>

== Technology and commerce ==
Zilingo started off as a mobile-first eCommerce marketplace and expanded into a B2B tech-platform. Their ''seller management platform'' offered small retailers and longtail brands online distribution, inventory management tools and APIs for logistics.<ref name="TechCrunch8" />

Their seller management tool became profitable by 2018, offering financial services, a “style hunter", product sourcing, and content / photography services. Zilingo's customer base expanded to include fashion sellers, SMEs,  Southeast Asian brands and B2B businesses.<ref name="TechCrunch54" />

Zilingo's tech assets were sold to Swiss firm Buyogo in January 2023.

extract: Zilingo was an ecommerce fashion platform founded in 2015 by Ankiti Bose and Dhruv Kapoor, with operations spanning India, Singapore, Indonesia, Hong Kong, Thailand, Philippines, Australia and the United States. The company once valued at close to one billion dollars ceased operations in 2022 amidst scandal and mismanagement.  It sold its tech assets to Swiss firm Buyogo in January 2023. It entered liquidation in February 2023 with sources indicating there was nothing left to be recovered.  Lawsuits related to the implosion of the business remain ongoing.
